Subject: Annual commit guidance and PO workflow

Hi Marissa,

We're preparing our 2027 vendor contracts and evaluating commit options for hosted inference. Can you share Redwood's standard annual commit tiers (Starter/Growth/Enterprise), the per-token discounts at each tier, and the procurement/PO process (what your billing team needs, lead times, DocuSign vs PO)? We expect token consumption to be uneven across quarters; would like to understand carry-forward or true-up mechanics.

Thanks,
Rajiv Shah
Head of Procurement
BrightWave Health

---
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: BrightWave Procurement <procurement@brightwave.com>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 15 Jul 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Annual commit guidance and PO workflow

Hi Rajiv — thanks for the note and the context. Short answer: we offer three structured annual commit options designed to match company scale and predictability: Starter, Growth, and Enterprise. High level:

- Starter: 0.6M tokens/month baseline (7.2M/yr) with 6% per-token discount vs list for the committed volume; true-up at year-end, no carry-forward.
- Growth: 3M tokens/month baseline (36M/yr) with 14% per-token discount for committed units; unused committed tokens are carry-forwardable up to one quarter and eligible for partial credit on renewal.
- Enterprise: custom commits (typically 200M+/yr) with tiered discounts (starts at 20% and steps to 30% at higher slabs), dedicated reporting, and SLA credits. Enterprise includes a 90-day runway for PO and invoicing windows we usually accept.

A few clarifying points for procurement:
- Billing: For annual commits we can invoice upfront (net-30) or on a quarterly schedule. Our Revenue Ops prefers a single PO referencing the deal id and the DocuSign packet; they will generate invoices against that PO.
- True-ups: We do year-end true-up for Starter and Growth. Growth supports limited quarterly carry-forward as noted. Enterprise terms are negotiated case-by-case.
- DocuSign vs PO: We accept either. DocuSign gets the deal into our contract system faster; POs are fine but we need the PO to reference the DocuSign or the signed SOW to avoid delays.

I'll attach a short one-pager that lays the numbers out and a suggested initial commitment schedule. Connor included some OPS notes below about burst handling and cost guardrails. Happy to walk through this on a quick call.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attach: Redwood_Commit_Tier_Summary.pdf

From: connor_obrien@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Annual commit guidance and PO workflow

Hi Rajiv — quick operational notes from the solutions side:

- If BrightWave expects bursty peaks, we recommend Growth with a burst allowance (typically +30% for short windows) or Enterprise with burst credits. Bursts are met from pooled capacity; we instrument cost caps per API key.
- Token pricing shown on the worksheet assumes our default tokenization (1 token ~ 4 characters). If you have long-document ingestion patterns we can adjust the effective unit pricing.
- For auditing and SOC2 evidence: we can include per-token transparency logs for Enterprise deals; Growth gets token-level summaries.

Ping me with expected monthly distribution and I can draft an example invoice schedule and burst policy language for the SOW.

Connor O'Brien
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
